analysis.title: Global Credit Trader: AI Related Supply: Outlining the Directional Risks
key_insights: Since October 29, five hyperscaler bond deals totaled $67 billion, taking hyperscalers' year-to-date global debt issuance to $296 billion, above GS's full-year 2026 forecast of $250 billion.

Year-to-date hyperscaler issuance equals 36% of the aggregate 2026 Capex forecast by GIR equity research, above GS's initial expectation of 33% debt funded. In some cases this reflects a pull-forward of planned 2027 supply.
GS sees scope for more front-loading of issuance, depending on market tone. Between now and early December, GS sees risks to its forecasts as firmly tilted toward more spread widening.
GS still expects 35% of hyperscalers' 2027 Capex to be debt financed, roughly $440 billion of direct issuance, plus an additional $300 billion of project finance issuance in 2027 across IG and HY.
GS believes the HY primary market may be in a 'price discovery' phase in the near term, with a sharp focus on structures for project finance deals once issuance resumes.

Delayed monetization and growth in purchase commitments, which GS treats as additional and sizable uses of cash separate from Capex, are the key risks to more debt issuance. Faster near-term monetization of AI investment is the key risk to less debt issuance.

GS economists say the US midterms outcome is less likely to change the outlook for data center and AI regulation. Short-term data center moratoriums are possible and could affect about 45% of planned US data center capacity expansion, with a large portion in Texas. They expect moratoriums to be short-lived.

Market participants treat AI-related issuers' capital structures as part of a holistic framework, since access to debt financing is seen as a strategic competitive advantage in funding the AI buildout.

sector_views.rationale: GS sees risks to its issuance forecasts tilted toward more spread widening through early December as supply runs ahead of its forecast.

risk_factors: Delayed monetization of AI investment could lead to more debt issuance.
Growth in purchase commitments adds sizable cash uses separate from Capex and could raise debt issuance.
Faster near-term monetization of AI investment is the key risk to less debt issuance.
Short-term data center moratoriums could affect about 45% of planned US data center capacity expansion, with a large portion in Texas.
Front-loading of issuance depends on market tone, and GS sees risks tilted toward more widening through early December.
